reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because the creator discusses BitConnect's shutdown and criticizes it as a suspected Ponzi scheme rather than soliciting viewers to invest. The creator warns viewers against promised daily returns, advises selling or avoiding BitConnect, and frames the discussion as a lesson about researching investments.

citations.quote: I've been trying to tell people for so long that this is a scam. It's a Ponzi scheme.
anybody that offers you daily returns is lying.
I just wanted to do a quick live stream
they're giving everyone back the money in their active investments.
especially if they're offering you daily returns, like BitConnect was.

opening.argument: The financial proposition is tied to participation in a lending platform and to recruitment. The discussion presents passive income and daily returns as the central attraction, while also describing profits generated from people who signed up through an affiliate link. That creates the recognizable promise-action structure: join or place funds in the platform, potentially earn recurring returns, and expand the participant base. The fact that the speaker disputes the claims does not erase that the video supplies the exact investment mechanism, return language, and affiliate pathway a viewer would need to understand how the scheme operates.

citations.quote: passive income and, like, incredible gains and being financially dependent.
You can't earn 1% a day on a platform like this.
all of the other profits that he gained off of it he just gained from all of the people that signed up using his affiliate link
especially if they're offering you daily returns, like BitConnect was.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the platform a scam is still an account of the same money-making proposition, not proof that the video lacks a solicitation pathway. The opening repeats passive-income, daily-return, affiliate, and lending details, and therefore makes participation legible. Advising viewers to sell or avoid it does not change that the video connects financial returns with platform activity and signups.

citations.quote: passive income and, like, incredible gains and being financially dependent.
all of the other profits that he gained off of it he just gained from all of the people that signed up using his affiliate link

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material explicitly rejects the alleged offer rather than making it. “You can't earn 1% a day” is a warning, and the affiliate statement attributes profits to promoters, not to a viewer being asked to join. Nothing in these excerpts asks viewers to deposit, lend, or recruit; describing a risky mechanism is not soliciting participation.

citations.quote: You can't earn 1% a day on a platform like this.
anybody that offers you daily returns is lying.
you should never trust anybody, especially if they're offering you daily returns

opening.argument: The combination of fixed-looking daily returns, passive-income framing, token valuation, and withdrawal failure is a concentrated investment red-flag pattern. The discussion refers to claims of 1% or 2% per day, says users could not withdraw BCC, and describes the platform as giving back value in a form worth less than the stated valuation. A BitConnect page is also visibly shown announcing immediate closure of its lending and exchange platforms. Taken together, the content depicts a lending investment whose promised returns and access to funds depend on the platform remaining operational, a structure strongly consistent with deceptive investment promotion.

citations.quote: anybody that promises 1% or 2% a day is lying.
I am a login but can't withdraw BCC coin.
you're going to to get a fraction of what you put into it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account treats these signals as neutral reporting, but the video repeatedly foregrounds exactly the inducements and failure conditions that make the financial offer deceptive: daily returns, lending, token conversion, and inaccessible withdrawals. Whether the speaker personally approves is less important than the investment proposition presented and the resulting money-flow risk.

citations.quote: Things that offer you daily returns by saying, oh, you'll make one or two percent a day on our platform
How do we get our money out? Uh, their site is not working. You can't
once the ICO sold out they decided to stop lending on their lending platform

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not unqualified promotional claims. The speaker says the daily-return promise is impossible, tells viewers to sell BCC, and describes the inability to withdraw as evidence that users were scammed. The frame shows a closure notice, but it does not establish that the speaker promises returns or invites investment; it supports the warning context instead.

citations.quote: anybody that offers you daily returns is lying.
Sell it as quickly as you can.
Unfortunately, you've been scammed

opening.argument: Although presented as commentary, the video also functions as market-direction content. It tells viewers that a low-price environment is a “really great time to buy,” recommends low-ball orders, and discusses the coin's exchange price and possible future market recovery. That turns an apparent warning into actionable token-market guidance: viewers are encouraged to purchase depressed crypto assets while the video supplies price context and upside expectations. The promotional role is especially clear because the speaker links market participation to buying opportunities rather than merely documenting the shutdown.

citations.quote: right now is a really great time to buy.
Just put some low-ball orders
this gives you buying opportunities guys. To buy coins at really low prices
by this summer we could see a two trillion dollar market cap hands down

rebuttal.rebuttal: The warning framing does not remove the video's operative call to buy. The speaker supplies timing, order guidance, and a bullish market projection, so viewers receive a concrete purchase rationale amid the BitConnect collapse. A segment can criticize one token while steering viewers toward speculative token buying generally; the practical effect remains promotion of risky participation.

citations.quote: right now is a really great time to buy.
this gives you buying opportunities guys. To buy coins at really low prices
Bitcoin is going to bounce back.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The buying comments concern the broader cryptocurrency market and are accompanied by explicit uncertainty, not a promise that a token will appreciate. The speaker says BCC cannot be sold, calls BitConnect a scam, and repeatedly tells viewers to research projects and invest at their own risk. Those statements undercut a reading that the BitConnect discussion promotes token purchase.

citations.quote: you're gonna be able to sell it at this point
invest at your own risk.
Do your research and find which projects are actually genuine.
Bit Connect is quitting.
